## Definition

The **dependent variable (DV)** is the variable that is measured in an experiment. It is the outcome that is expected to change as a result of manipulating the independent variable. It is the presumed *effect* in a cause-and-effect relationship.

## Key Characteristics

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Measured | Observed and recorded |
| Presumed effect | Expected to be influenced by IV |
| Depends on IV | Changes in response to manipulation |
| Quantified | Expressed in measurable units |

## Operationalising the DV

The DV must be clearly defined and measurable:

| Concept | Operationalised DV | Units |
|---------|-------------------|-------|
| Memory | Number of words recalled | Count |
| Attention | Reaction time | Milliseconds |
| Mood | Score on questionnaire | 1-10 scale |
| Performance | Accuracy percentage | % correct |

## Identifying the DV

Ask: "What is being measured?"

> "Does caffeine improve **memory**?"

DV = Memory (operationalised as number of words recalled)

> "Does music affect **concentration**?"

DV = Concentration (operationalised as task accuracy)

## Properties of a Good DV

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Reliable | Consistent measurement |
| Valid | Measures what it claims to |
| Sensitive | Can detect real differences |
| Objective | Not biased by expectations |

## Multiple DVs

Studies can measure more than one DV:

```
Research question: Effect of caffeine on cognition

DV1: Reaction time (ms)
DV2: Accuracy (% correct)
DV3: Subjective alertness (1-10)
```

## Common DV Types in Psychology

| DV Type | Examples |
|---------|----------|
| Behavioural | Reaction time, choices made |
| Self-report | Questionnaire scores, ratings |
| Physiological | Heart rate, cortisol levels |
| Performance | Accuracy, number correct |

## DataLab Connection

At the **Reflex Test**, the DV is reaction time measured in milliseconds. At **Time Warp**, the DV is the estimated time in seconds. Clear operationalisation ensures everyone measures the same thing.
